issues.description: The problem text explicitly instructs students to implement the Animal name getter and setter with protected visibility, but the reference solution declares getName() and setName() as public. This mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about the intended access level and may cause test expectations or grading scripts to disagree with the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility of the Animal name accessor methods consistent with the problem statement. Either update the solution's Animal.getName() and Animal.setName(...) to be protected, or change the problem statement to explicitly require public accessors. Preferably, change the solution to use protected getters and setters to match the specification in the problem text.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement indicates the Animal constructor should be protected (UML shows '#' visibility), while the solution implements a public Animal(String) constructor. This creates an inconsistency between the UML specification and the provided solution that may confuse students about intended constructor visibility.
issues.suggestedFix: Align constructor visibility with the UML and problem text. Either change the Animal constructor in the solution to protected (protected Animal(String name)) to match the UML, or update the UML/problem statement to state the constructor is public. Prefer changing the solution constructor to protected if the exercise aims to teach protected members/constructors.
